title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 1st District
area: Southern Minnesota, including Rochester, Mankato, Austin, Owatonna and the region along the Iowa border.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Brad Finstad (R) is unopposed in the Republican primary and faces Jake Johnson, who won the Democratic primary, in the general election.

candidates.name: Brad Finstad

summary.text: Brad Finstad is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Minnesota's 1st Congressional District. He has represented the district since winning a 2022 special election and previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives.

background.text: Born in New Ulm, Minnesota, in 1976; earned a degree in agriculture education from the University of Minnesota-Twin Cities.

Worked as a staffer for U.S. Rep. Mark Kennedy (R), as state director for rural development at the U.S. Department of Agriculture, and as executive director of the Minnesota Turkey Growers Association and of the Center for Rural Policy & Development.
Served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2003 to 2009.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (chair of the Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture subcommittee), the House Committee on Small Business, and the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately; this entry focuses on biography, committee roles and record.

candidates.name: Jake Johnson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary over Alex Eaton.

summary.text: Jake Johnson is the Democratic nominee challenging Rep. Brad Finstad. He is a high school math teacher from Rochester running on lowering costs, opposing corporate influence in politics, and investing in small towns.

background.text: Grew up in Stewartville, Minnesota, one of eleven siblings, the son of a garbage collector and a meter reader.
Has taught high school math in Rochester for about 20 years.
Has worked as a government relations coordinator and served on the board of the Minnesota Jump$tart Coalition, focused on financial literacy for kids.
Lives in Southern Minnesota with his wife Molly, a paraprofessional, raising four sons.

priorities.text: Bringing down costs: opposes broad tariffs and says he would vote to end them; supports cutting red tape on home building and childcare; opposes corporate PAC money and says he'll take on corporate monopolies and health insurers.
Taking on corruption: supports a balanced-budget amendment, term limits, a ban on members of Congress trading stocks or becoming lobbyists, and a ban on pardons for family members and donors.

Investing in small towns: supports passing a bipartisan farm bill, a 'right to repair' for farm equipment, protecting Social Security, Medicare and veterans' benefits, and reversing recent cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

positions.summary: Says he would vote to end broad tariffs that he argues are driving up the price of groceries, gas and fertilizer.
Supports extending tax credits for health insurance and reversing recent cuts to Medicaid (Medical Assistance).
Supports tax cuts for working families and small businesses paid for by raising taxes and closing loopholes for large corporations and the wealthiest earners.
Supports cutting regulatory red tape so homes can be built more quickly.
